title: Regulating Free-scalar and Yang--Lee 5d CFTs on the Fuzzy Four Sphere
abstract: Non-commutative sphere regularization of CFT has become a powerful tool for computing conformal data of 3d CFTs and was recently extended to 4d CFTs. In this work we further construct 5d free-scalar CFT and Yang-Lee CFT on a fuzzy 4-sphere. We observe a continuous phase transition and conformal towers in these examples. We obtain the first three scalar primaries of the 5d free-scalar CFT, furthermore, we compute the 5d Yang-Lee $Δ_φ,Δ_{φ^3}$ with $N_e=10$ fermions using exact diagonalization (ED) and $N_e=20$ fermions using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG), obtaining relatively good agreement with both $ε$-expansion and the Gliozzi truncated bootstrap result.
summary: This work investigates 5D CFTs (Free-scalar and Yang-Lee) regularized on the Fuzzy Four Sphere. By employing advanced numerical techniques like DMRG, the authors demonstrate continuous phase transitions and calculate key conformal dimensions. This provides a theoretical framework for understanding critical behavior in complex quantum field theories.
main_problem: The paper constructs and analyzes 5D Free-scalar and Yang-Lee Conformal Field Theories (CFTs) regularized on the Fuzzy Four Sphere.
main_result: The study confirms the existence of continuous phase transitions and conformal towers in these models, yielding scaling dimensions consistent with established CFT results.
method: The analysis employs advanced numerical techniques like Exact Diagonalization (ED) and Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) to compute energy spectra and scaling dimensions.
model_or_system: The models are defined on a fuzzy 4-sphere ($S^4$) and include a free-scalar CFT (Ising model) and a Yang-Lee CFT, both governed by specific Hamiltonians derived using $SO(5)$ invariance.
key_observables: Scaling dimensions ($\Delta_\phi, \Delta_{\phi^3}$), energy spectra ($E_n - E_0$), and the observation of continuous phase transitions.
important_parameters: The coupling constant $h_x$ (for phase transition tuning) and the fermion number $N_e$ (for DMRG calculations).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the fuzzy sphere regularization method and assumes the applicability of CFT correspondence between the low-energy spectrum and the continuum theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagrams for the Yang-Lee model, energy level splittings at critical points, and the cost functions used to match calculated spectra to CFT predictions.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the construction of the 5D CFTs on the fuzzy $S^4$, details the Hamiltonians for the free-scalar and Yang-Lee models, and then applies ED and DMRG to calculate spectra, observe phase transitions, and extract scaling dimensions.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of numerical methods like DMRG to study critical phenomena and CFTs on non-trivial manifolds like the fuzzy sphere provides advanced techniques applicable to strongly correlated quantum systems.
